newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT--Dollar struggles within familiar ranges.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT--Dollar struggles within familiar ranges.

text.p: The dollar crept back toward significant resistance levels Thursday, notably against the mark, and could muster another run toward the upside in coming sessions, technical analysts said.
After a brief tumble Wednesday, the dollar held recent support nicely and rebounded, leaving it once again staring at resistance in the 1.5165/75 marks area.
"It's like a rock up there," said John Tirone, technical analyst at Chase Securities Inc.
Yet for all its recent gyrations, the dollar remains pinned in a narrow range on an opening and closing basis.
Over the last nine trading sessions, the dollar has opened and closed no higher than 1.5088 marks and no lower than 1.5145, highlighting the dollar's inertia, chartists said.
"We've got a pretty well-defined upside and we've had trouble closing below 1.5080 (marks)," Tirone said.
Beyond the 1.5165/75 level, which roughly matches a two-month high, stands fresh resistance at 1.5260, another key high from July, technical analysts said.
"The recovery from Wednesday's losses keeps the focus on the upside," said Pete Grant, senior foreign exchange analyst at MMS International.

Against the yen, the dollar remains weakened after failing to hold 110 this week. Computer-driven selling triggered en masse after the break Wednesday left the dollar bruised and vulnerable, analysts said.
"I suspect we'll at least test back below 109 yen. The move was a bit impulsive yesterday and we're starting to see a bear flag on the hourly chart," Grant said.
But the dollar should find 108.60/70 yen well-fortified, and could soon make another rally, technicians said. If it can hold 109.50, the road will then open to 110.60.

Mark/yen looks far more solid in the low 72 range than it did above 73, with a near-term objective at 72.55. If the cross sustains that level, a retest of the 73.30 level looks likely, chartists said.
"Support at 72.05 remains intact. I don't think 73 is out of the question," Grant said.
Meanwhile, cable looks suddenly vulnerable after plunging to a 19-day low Thursday.
"Sterling had a nice reversal (Wednesday) and got as high as $1.5640. Then baboom, today just crushed it," said Tirone.
